properties.alert_text_en: Damaging winds are no longer expected.

The first notable snowfall of the season is expected.  

Locations: Eagle River, Cartwright to Black Tickle, Norman Bay to Lodge Bay, and Red Bay to L'Anse-au-Clair.

Potential snowfall: 5 to 10 cm inland and over higher terrain.

Time span: Saturday.

Remarks: A developing low pressure system is expected to bring a period of accumulating snow. The snow is expected to be wet and heavy. Snow accumulation may make travel slow or hazardous. Roads could become slippery and difficult to navigate.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

Fall Storm Bringing Mixed Weather Conditions this Saturday.

What:
- Sudden gusty winds of 60 to 80 km/h.
- Snow levels lowering to 1500 metres over southern B.C.
- Snow levels lowering to 1200 metres over central B.C.
- Risk of thunderstorms over Cariboo and Columbia regions.

When:
Saturday except this morning for the Chilcotin.

Where:
- Fraser Valley East including Hope
- Coquihalla Highway - Hope to Kamloops
- Highway 97C - Okanagan Connector
- Highway 3 - Hope to Princeton via Allison Pass
- Manning - Skagit Valley
- Similkameen
- Nicola
- 100 Mile
- Chilcotin
- Cariboo
- Prince George
- Stuart - Nechako
- Lakes District

Impacts:
- Possible localised utility outages
- Possible fallen branches
- High profile vehicles should take caution in high winds
- Possible slippery conditions over high elevation passes with wet snow

Additional information:
A sharp cold front moving across the B.C. Interior on Saturday will primarily generate strong gusty winds of 60 to 80 km/h. Ahead of this cold front, strong southwest winds gusting to 80 km/h will develop lee of the Coast Mountains in the Chilcotin this morning. Snow levels will fall with the passage of this cold front on Saturday and may produce some snow over high elevation highway passes. In the wake of the cold front, cold and unstable air will generate scattered showers, small hail and risk of thunderstorms across the central interior and parts of the Columbia regions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
